sections.skill: Use examples to show what you want, and notice when they pull too hard

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: Why include a short example of the desired output?

choices.text: It shows the style, length and structure to copy
It makes the reply arrive faster than usual
It proves the facts in the answer are true
It makes the tool ignore all other instructions

questions.correct_answer: It shows the style, length and structure to copy
questions.intro: Sometimes the fastest way to explain what you want is to SHOW it. Adding one or two short EXAMPLES of the desired output, such as a sample product description or a sample quiz question, helps the tool copy the style, length and structure. But examples are powerful: the tool may copy them too closely, repeating their topic, length or wording even when your written instructions say otherwise. Use examples that match what you want, label them clearly ("Example of the style I want:"), and say what should differ ("use new topics, not the example's topic").
questions.feedback: Examples demonstrate the pattern.

sections.skill: Compare examples with a sample a tailor copies

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: What does the tailor copy from the sample shirt?

choices.text: Its fit, collar and length
Only the store it came from
Only its price tag
Nothing at all

questions.correct_answer: Its fit, collar and length
questions.intro: If you bring a TAILOR your favorite shirt and say "make one like this," the tailor copies its fit, collar and length. That is helpful. But if you wanted a DIFFERENT color and forgot to say so, you may get the same color too, because the sample shows everything, not only the parts you meant. A tailor also tends to trust the shirt in hand over a quick comment. Examples in a request work the same way: they show a lot, and the tool may copy more than you intended.
questions.feedback: Samples show many features.

sections.skill: Fix conflicts between examples and instructions

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: Instructions say "four sentences each," but the only example has two sentences. What result is likely?

choices.text: Descriptions in a different language
Short descriptions that follow the example
No descriptions at all
Exactly four sentences every time

questions.correct_answer: Short descriptions that follow the example
questions.intro: When written instructions and examples disagree, the example often wins. If your instructions say "write four-sentence descriptions" but your only example has two sentences, expect short results. If every example mentions the same product, the tool may keep mentioning it. Fix conflicts by changing the example to match the rules, giving two varied examples instead of one, or removing the example and describing the pattern in words. Then check that results follow the rules, not just the example.
questions.feedback: Examples tend to override conflicting rules.
